text:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a small A100 vs H100 pass for the 7B bring‑up. Prefill=512 / decode=256 workloads, looked at fp16 + q4 variants, batch sizes 1/4/8. dropping raw numbers below. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

mira: awesome — did you run in multiple regions or same zone snapshot? any kernel differences?

alex: ran us-west2 on A100 (40GB) and eu-west1 on H100 (80GB) to reflect our typical customer split. kernels: flash_attn when available, fallback to triton/nvfusion for q kernels. same docker image + runtime flags.

jamie: summary (p95-like view, single-run medians):

```
Model: open-7b-fork
Workload: prefill=512 + decode=256 (tokens measured on decode window)
Kernel variants: flash_attn | triton
Regions: us-west2 (A100) / eu-west1 (H100)

Batch=1:
  A100 fp16  : prefill= 92 ms | decode= 24 ms | tok/s=1.6k  | $/1M ≈ $12.3
  H100 fp16  : prefill= 64 ms | decode= 18 ms | tok/s=2.1k  | $/1M ≈ $9.0
  A100 q4f   : prefill=110 ms | decode= 36 ms | tok/s=1.9k  | $/1M ≈ $8.4
  H100 q4f   : prefill= 78 ms | decode= 26 ms | tok/s=2.6k  | $/1M ≈ $6.1

Batch=8 (amortized prefill across batch):
  A100 fp16  : prefill=180 ms | decode=110 ms | tok/s=7.2k  | $/1M ≈ $2.7
  H100 fp16  : prefill=120 ms | decode= 78 ms | tok/s=9.5k  | $/1M ≈ $2.0
  A100 q4f   : prefill=210 ms | decode=130 ms | tok/s=8.1k  | $/1M ≈ $2.4
  H100 q4f   : prefill=150 ms | decode= 95 ms | tok/s=10.4k | $/1M ≈ $1.8

Notes: numbers are median of 5 runs. cost estimates use on-demand list price + our estimated infra efficiency (batching, multiplexing) and include token accounting for both prefill+decode. KV-cache warm hits reduced decode ~10% on H100 runs.
```

chris: command used for runs (same runtime flags we use in CI):

```
./run_infer.sh \
  --model open-7b \
  --quant q4f \
  --kernel flash_attn \
  --prefill 512 \
  --decode 256 \
  --batch 1 \
  --region us-west2 \
  --emit-metrics /tmp/metrics.json
```

mira: good context — what about warm-cache vs cold-cache for prefill? also, did you try q4a vs q4f differences on H100?

alex: warm vs cold: cold prefill adds ~12–18% to prefill latency at batch=1 on both GPUs. For q formats: q4f consistently better on H100 because our fused kernels map registers better; q4a had slightly smaller model size but triggered more triton fallbacks in our runtime which increased latency by ~15% in decode.

perf-bot: automated summary: H100 wins across prefills and decode for both fp16 and q4f; quant helps both, but H100's kernel maturity (flash_attn + fused q kernels) gives larger relative win.

jamie: actionable next steps: 1) run regional parity (us-east/us-west/eu) with identical kernel sets to isolate iso-kernel impact; 2) sweep batch sizes 2/4/16 for throughput curves; 3) add reserved pricing scenarios to $/1M token calc.

chris: agree. also add a small eval set to check quality delta between fp16 and q4f (we saw subtle tokenization differences in a few prompts).

mira: I'll queue a 48h sweep in perf infra, include q4a/q4f/fp16 and both kernels. will attach results here when done. :white_check_mark:

alex: perfect — thanks team. saving logs to s3://redwood-perf/7b/1795001234/ ; link -> <https://s3.redwood/perf/7b/1795001234> (private).

jamie: noted — if H100 gains are consistent at tail, we should recommend H100 for latency-sensitive tiers and A100 reserved capacity for cost-sensitive sustained throughput customers.

mira: adding an item to the onboarding checklist: confirm kernel maturity for new quant builds before marking model "production-ready".

alex: +1. closing this thread, will reopen with sweep output. :rocket:
